steps.instruction: Crack the eggs into a large jug or mixing bowl. Add a pinch of salt and whisk well until combined. Sift in the plain flour and whisk until you have a smooth, lump-free paste. Gradually pour in the milk, whisking continuously, until you have a smooth batter the consistency of single cream. Leave the batter to rest for at least 30 minutes at room temperature — this is important for light, puffy Yorkshires.

steps.summary: Heat the oil in the tin
steps.instruction: Put about half a teaspoon of sunflower oil into each hole of a 12-hole muffin tin (or a Yorkshire pudding tin). Place in the oven at 220°C fan for at least 5 minutes until the oil is smoking hot. The oil must be very hot — this is the key to getting the puddings to rise.

Working quickly — do not let the tin cool down — carefully remove the tin from the oven and pour the batter evenly into the holes, filling each one about one-third full. The batter should sizzle as it hits the hot oil. Return the tin to the oven immediately.

Bake at 220°C fan for 20–25 minutes until the Yorkshire puddings are puffed up, golden brown, and crispy. Do NOT open the oven door during baking — even a brief opening can cause them to collapse. They should be well risen, golden, and hollow in the middle.
